item.content:encoded: I thought this was really well done. Personally, I thought the tone worked really well, but I know thats a matter of opinion based on headcanons of parawatch etc. In any case the story was really well written and quite gripping. Great job!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Thank you! I see how it would work without Parawatch, but my love for the GOI and the familiarity bonus it brings is why I still keep it here. Future projects might not use the CSS but this one will because that's how I wrote this one in particular.

I was inspired by a 2017 Bogleech creepypasta contestant piece, called Gut Alley, for the style of prose, although it deviated as I wrote it. That might explain the tone sounding foreign to Parawatch.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Good shit. ARD's comment sounds like what someone would comment in the thread on the Parawatch forums, using it as evidence to disprove the story. So, in a sense I agree. In another, I don't particularly care. I think that the dark background with white text is really perfect for the tone of creepypasta, and this hits that creepypasta vibe in prose and execution. I know some people have had a hard time with this CSS, but I love it.

If it affects you at all, I do think this could work just as well without the forum CSS. Like, if you decide it really doesn't make sense as a Parawatch forum piece, you wouldn't have to change a single word to make that port over. Anyways, +1 obviously.

EDIT: And happy first article!!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: That is interesting. Tone was something that came fairly naturally while writing but clashed with the medium. In the future, I'll definitely keep that in mind, the framing and medium affecting prose in that way. Thank you for the criticism.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This isn't bad. Lines like "That still, in that direction, my uncle waits, among the crown of horns." and phrases like "I bolted wild through the night," are much more suited to dark urban fantasy or even gothic horror than the semi-realistic fiction tone that a Parawatch piece ought to go for. It makes for a good horror piece but a bad Parawatch piece.
